title: Intermittent tail-latency regression from scheduler+kselector interaction
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: After a staged rollout of the new scheduler heuristics (runtime-2.4.0-rc), multiple customer-facing capacity events were reported as sporadic high p95/p99 tail latency for generation workloads. Investigation shows a timing-based interaction between the scheduler's request coalescing window and the new kernel selector scoring that caused increased KV-cache misses and suboptimal kernel choices for medium-length sequences. The behavior is intermittent and correlated with bursty small-batch traffic and attention streaming usage. Impact: elevated p99 (up to 3x baseline) for select model+seq combos, increased token egress cost, and customer incidents for latency-sensitive endpoints. Root cause hypothesis: the scheduler's tighter batching window pushed packets into ephemeral batches where the kernel selector incorrectly preferred a quantized matmul kernel optimized for long sequences; when attention-streaming toggles triggered partial KV cache invalidation, execution fell back to a less efficient kernel path and incurred cache thrash and extra memcpy overheads. This path hadn't been exercised in integration because unit tests used fixed sequence lengths and synthetic load patterns.
action_items: Hotfix: revert scheduler coalescing window change on runtime-2.4.0-rc across affected regions (rollback patch deployed 2026-03-10) - OWNER: Lucas
Short-term: add a runtime feature flag to disable the new kernel scoring for models using attention streaming and medium sequences - OWNER: SRE team

Telemetry: add histogram and labels to kernel-selection metrics (chosen_kernel, seq_len_bucket, batch_size, attention_streaming_flag) and capture KV-cache hit/miss counts per request - OWNER: Observability
Test: add integration load tests that combine bursty small-batch arrivals + attention-streaming to CI (stress harness with randomized coalescing timings) - OWNER: QA
Selector fix: adjust kernel-scoring penalty for kernel mismatch to weigh estimated KV-cache locality; add unit tests for mixed seq lengths - OWNER: Runtime team
Canary plan: gated rollout with traffic-split by sequence-length buckets and active SLO monitoring, hold at 5% for 48h then 25% for 24h if no regressions - OWNER: Release Engineering
Postmortem doc: produce a full timeline and RCA summarizing traces, affected customers, and cost impact for exec review - OWNER: Maya
decisions: Rollback scheduler coalescing window in prod immediately (done 2026-03-10)
Introduce kernel selection feature-flagging for streaming-sensitive models
Prioritize telemetry and synthetic test coverage before re-enabling heuristic in controlled canary
